Posterior sampling for discrete Markov random fields

Source: R/dmrfit_bayes.R
dmrfit_bayes.Rd

Bayesian inference for a discrete Markov random field (Ising or ordinal) by Markov chain Monte Carlo. By default, the posterior is approximated by the coordinate-rescaled (CoRe) pseudo-posterior of Arena and Marsman (2026): the pseudo-posterior rescaled around its mode so that its covariance matches the Godambe-Huber-White (GHW) covariance, which corrects the underestimated posterior variability of the pseudo-likelihood. All samplers use the Fisher adaptive Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (FisherMALA; Titsias, 2024).

dmrfit_bayes(
  data,
  parinit = NULL,
  method = c("core", "adacore", "exact", "dmh"),
  scale = c("ghw", "mch", "rm"),
  nsim = 1000,
  burnin = 1000,
  ncores = 1,
  thresholds_alpha = 0.5,
  thresholds_beta = 0.5,
  interactions_location = 0,
  interactions_scale = 2.5,
  sigma2 = 0.1,
  seed = 123,
  progress = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

data

data matrix, with rows as samples and columns as variables. Each variable should be rescaled to the range of 0 to m-1, where m is the number of categories for that variable. The baseline category is always the minimum value in the variable. The internal processing will check if the variables are rescaled and will rescale them if necessary. If there are any NAs in the data, they will be removed before optimization (listwise deletion).

parinit

initial parameter values for the optimization that finds the pseudo-posterior mode, a vector of length equal to the number of parameters in the model, sum(n_categories - 1) + P * (P - 1) / 2, where P is the number of variables. If NULL (default), a vector of zeros.

method

the sampler: "core" (default) samples the CoRe pseudo-posterior with a fixed rescaling matrix; "adacore" adapts the rescaling matrix during burn-in at the running mean of the draws; "exact" samples the posterior based on the full likelihood, whose normalizing constant is computed by enumerating all response patterns (only for small networks, see control); "dmh" samples the posterior based on the full likelihood with the double Metropolis-Hastings algorithm (Liang, 2010). DMH simulates auxiliary data at every iteration and is much slower than the other methods (minutes to hours instead of seconds, depending on the network size and control$dmh_aux); "core" runs at the cost of the pseudo-posterior sampler.

scale

the covariance to which the pseudo-posterior is rescaled, only used when method = "core": "ghw" (default) the Godambe-Huber-White (GHW) covariance; "mch" the inverse of the negative Hessian of the full log-posterior at the pseudo-posterior mode, estimated by Monte Carlo simulation; "rm" the same Hessian at the full-posterior mode, estimated by a Newton-type Robbins-Monro algorithm (the sampler remains centered at the pseudo-posterior mode). "mch" and "rm" simulate data from the model and are slower.

nsim

number of posterior draws kept after burn-in. Default is 1000.

burnin

number of burn-in iterations, after an initial adaptive stage of control$adaptive_stage iterations. Default is 1000.

ncores

number of cores used to compute the gradient, Hessian and pseudo-likelihood in parallel when finding the pseudo-posterior mode. It is capped at the number of available cores minus one, and has no effect when the package was built without OpenMP support. Default is 1.

thresholds_alpha

alpha parameter for the Beta-Prime prior on thresholds (default is 0.5).

thresholds_beta

beta parameter for the Beta-Prime prior on thresholds (default is 0.5).

interactions_location

location parameter for the Cauchy prior on pairwise interactions (default is 0.0).

interactions_scale

scale parameter for the Cauchy prior on pairwise interactions (default is 2.5).

sigma2

initial value for the adaptive variance parameter in the FisherMALA sampler (default is 0.1).

seed

random seed for reproducibility of the MCMC sampler (default is 123). The caller's random number stream is restored on exit.

progress

logical, whether to show a progress bar while sampling (default is TRUE).

control

a list of tuning settings, each with a default: adaptive_stage (500) iterations of the initial adaptive stage; max_states (1e6) largest number of response patterns for method = "exact"; dmh_aux (25000) and dmh_gibbs_iter (5) auxiliary draws and Gibbs sweeps per iteration of method = "dmh"; mc_draws (1e5) and mc_gibbs_iter (5) simulated observations and Gibbs sweeps for scale = "mch" and "rm"; rm_iter (50) Robbins-Monro iterations for scale = "rm".

Value

an object of class dmrfit_bayes (also of class dmrfit), including the pseudo-posterior mode (argument), the posterior draws (draws, a matrix with parameters by rows and iterations by columns), the acceptance rate (acceptance), the sampling method and scale (method, scale), the Savage-Dickey Bayes factors with the effective sample size of each parameter (savage_dickey), and the multivariate effective sample size of the draws (mess; Vats, Flegal and Jones, 2019), which is NA when there are fewer than P + 1 batches of floor(sqrt(nsim)) draws per parameter.

References

Arena, G. and Marsman, M. (2026). Bayesian inference for discrete Markov random fields through coordinate rescaling. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2601.17205

Liang, F. (2010). A double Metropolis-Hastings sampler for spatial models with intractable normalizing constants. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation, 80(9), 1007-1022.

Titsias, M. K. (2024). Optimal preconditioning and Fisher adaptive Langevin sampling. In Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS '23). Red Hook, NY, USA: Curran Associates.

Vats, D., Flegal, J. M., and Jones, G. L. (2019). Multivariate output analysis for Markov chain Monte Carlo. Biometrika, 106(2), 321-337.

See also

dmrfit for point estimation and Bayes factors by sampling importance resampling.

Examples


# binary responses of 1000 observations on 3 nodes (independent, for illustration)
set.seed(123)
n <- 1000
P <- 3
prob <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3)[rep(1:P, each = n)]
data <- matrix(rbinom(n * P, size = 1, prob = prob), nrow = n, ncol = P)
fit <- dmrfit_bayes(data = data, nsim = 500, burnin = 500, progress = FALSE)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> dmrfit_bayes(data = data, nsim = 500, burnin = 500, progress = FALSE)
#> 
#> Thresholds (posterior mode):
#> mu[1,1] mu[2,1] mu[3,1] 
#> -1.4423  0.0164 -0.8828 
#> 
#> Pairwise interactions (posterior mode):
#> theta[2,1] theta[3,1] theta[3,2] 
#>    -0.1374     0.3445    -0.0040 
#> 
#> Posterior: coordinate-rescaled pseudo-posterior (Godambe-Huber-White covariance) 
#> MCMC samples: 500  Acceptance rate: 0.6  Elapsed: 0 sec
#> Multivariate effective sample size: 236.1 
#> 
summary(fit)

# small network: the exact posterior is also available
fit_exact <- dmrfit_bayes(data = data, method = "exact", nsim = 500, burnin = 500, progress = FALSE)
summary(fit_exact)
